key_insight: Vision-language models can invent medical diagnoses even when no image is provided, and those guesses shift systematically with the patient demographic described.
clinical_relevance: In clinical workflows, this means structured outputs from multimodal AI should be audited directly because missing-image confabulation and demographic sensitivity could mislead downstream use.
method: Queried Claude Opus-4.7, GPT-5.4, and Gemini-3.1-Pro without attaching images.
Tested chest X-ray, brain MRI, and dermatology prompts across different demographic descriptors.
Compared how the returned diagnoses changed when only the demographic wording or probe word changed.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic effects across multiple demographic cells, with especially strong findings such as nearly universal melanoma for one dermatology prompt and frequent sarcoidosis for young Black patients on chest X-ray.
watch_item: A major implementation concern is that hedged prose may hide a conflicting structured diagnosis field, so evaluations must inspect the machine-readable output channel, not just the narrative.
paper_title: Hearsay: Vision-Language Medical Diagnoses Without an Image
